title: Traversal across a tape layer
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine with $k$ work tapes, let $x$ be a finite binary string, let $n,T,t\in\mathbb N$, and let $z$ be a finite binary string. Suppose $1\le T$ and $t\le T$. For any $d,\tau\in\mathbb N$ and register record $e$, assume $\tau+d=k$, $e$ records $n$ as its circuit-input count, $|z|$ as its hard-wired input length, and $T$ as its step budget, and that its current instruction index is $t\,\mathrm{Str}(M,n,z,T)+\tau(2T+1)$, its previous-cell index is $0$ when $t=0$ and otherwise the current index minus $\mathrm{Str}(M,n,z,T)$, its first-instruction-of-step index is $t\,\mathrm{Str}(M,n,z,T)$, and its inner-loop and scratch registers are both zero. Then, for every input position $p\in\mathbb N$, the counter program started at the beginning of the cell indexed by $\tau$ reaches the input-position phase with the same input position and register record obtained from $e$ by adding $d(2T+1)$ to the current instruction index and updating the previous-cell index to $0$ if $t=0$, or otherwise to the new instruction index minus $\mathrm{Str}(M,n,z,T)$. During this run it appends the concatenation of the instruction encodings for indices from the original current index through the next $d(2T+1)-1$ indices, and the run takes at most $d(2T+3)(L_{\max}(M)+20)$ steps.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Turing machine with Boolean symbols
$x$ is a finite Boolean input string
$n,T,t\in\mathbb N$ and $z$ is a finite Boolean string
